einzeiler: Chef Nina Compton on St. Lucia, Top Chef, and running restaurants in New Orleans.
kurzfassung: Chef Nina Compton discusses her culinary roots in St. Lucia and her journey to opening acclaimed restaurants in New Orleans. She reflects on her time as a fan favorite on Top Chef and the emotional community support she received. Compton also shares her vision for mentoring female chefs and empowering the Caribbean food industry.
stichpunkte: Grew up in St. Lucia surrounded by a bustling kitchen culture and abundant fresh local produce
Started her professional career at Sandals resort at age 19, working through holidays and grueling hours
Gained national recognition as a runner-up and fan favorite on Top Chef, turning defeat into a cultural victory
Faced massive local demand for her signature goat dish, quickly overwhelming her primary supplier
Uses Caribbean rum broadly in European-style cooking techniques despite its underutilization in American kitchens
Closed her casual pasta spot during the pandemic to prioritize personal health and mental well-being
Founded Ladies Night NOLA to highlight and support female-owned and run restaurants in New Orleans
Plans to eventually return to the Caribbean to establish culinary training programs and empower local talent

beschreibung:
The James Beard-winning chef on life after Top Chef, building Compère Lapin and realizing a restaurant was never worth sacrificing herself for.
Nina Compton became a fan favorite on Top Chef, but what happened after the finale may be the more interesting part of her story.
Nina sits down with Noël Burgess to talk about growing up in St. Lucia, representing the Caribbean on national television and eventually building Compère Lapin in New Orleans.
She remembers just how seriously St. Lucia took that Top Chef finale, including why Tom Colicchio might have wanted to avoid the island for a while. Nina also talks about the people who kept telling her she should have won and why, looking back, she feels like she did.
Then the conversation gets into what came next. Building restaurants. Closing Bywater American Bistro. Watching people around her sacrifice their health for the business. And reaching the point where Nina realized, in her words, "I'm not going to die for a restaurant."
There is plenty of food too. Nina gets into what people misunderstand about Caribbean cooking, curried goat taking over the kitchen, why she reaches for rum instead of white wine and the New Orleans restaurants she actually likes visiting when she gets the chance.
